messages.author: 760d13932202d6cf
messages.subject: compile pdf without R
parts:
Hi,

I am wondering if there is a possibility to compile a pdf document without evaluating R chunks enclosed with <<>>= @
Why I need it, it is because now I am writing a text, and from time to time I want to produce a pdf that other people can read, but I do not want to rerun everything including the R code. 
R chunks were previously evaluated, some of them cached some not.  

Or maybe there is a better routine?

Thanks,
Olga

messages.author: b256a2742aacd200
messages.subject: Re: compile pdf without R
parts:
You will get what you want if you have latexmk installed and if you put the text in another document and input it in the main document. Example:

\input{MoreText.tex}

When you do <LocalLeader>kp in the MainDocument.Rnw, the Vim-R-plugin will not call knit() because the .Rnw document didn't change, but it will call latexmk to build the PDF and the latexmk application will follow the \input{} links and detect when there was changes in them.

parts: Thanks, I was not aware of latexmk functionality. That's a clever solution, at least for bigger pieces of text, but for smaller ones it does require some fiddling.
